column3: “Became son-in-law with Pharaoh” is rendered “formed a marriage alliance with Pharaoh.”
“Making smoke” is rendered “burned incense”; “only” is rendered “except.”
“Ask what I will give you” is rendered “Ask what you wish me to give you.”
“A young lad” is rendered “a little child,” and NASB adds “how.”
“A listening heart” is rendered “an understanding heart,” and “massive” as “great.”
“Many days” is rendered “long life,” and “to understand to hear judgment” as “discernment to understand justice.”
The Hebrew present (“I do … I give”) is rendered “I have done … I have given.”
“I give” is rendered “I have also given.”
NASB supplies “a child” and “while she was.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB adds “because.”
NASB names “the first woman” for “this one.”
“Her compassions grew warm” is rendered “she was deeply stirred.”
